sentences.text: Leptostyrax was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, the group containing all sharks, rays, and skates.
This species belongs to the family Eoptolamnidae, a parent group of ancient sharks.
Vertebrae suggest the shark reached lengths of 6.3 to 8.3 meters, potentially making it one of the largest Cretaceous sharks.
Its tearing type dentition indicates a preference for moderately large prey such as bony fishes.
The genus Leptostyrax was first described by Williston in 1900.
The type species of the genus is Leptostyrax macrorhiza.
Leptostyrax stychi is a valid species within the genus, described by Schmitz, Thies, and Kriwet in 2010.
Leptostyrax lived from the Barremian to the Bartonian stages, between 125.77 and 37.71 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in North America, Europe, Africa, and Australia.
It is considered one of the earliest known lamniform sharks that underwent an adaptive radiation in the Early Cretaceous.
